title.zh: 终态分子离子密度与温度归约

summary: Reduce caller-supplied H2 and neutral densities, ion temperature and rate profiles to terminal H2+ density, temperature, dissociation and energy-exchange profiles.

capability: Reduce caller-supplied H2 and neutral densities, ion temperature and rate profiles to terminal H2+ density, temperature, dissociation and energy-exchange profiles.
operation: aligned x profiles and an eleven-channel reaction table -> four x profiles
discovery.model: terminal molecular-ion algebraic state reduction with caller-supplied rate table
discovery.geometry: one-dimensional spatial cell profiles; no velocity-grid input or iteration
discovery.boundary: finite aligned nonempty profiles; nonnegative molecular and neutral densities, ionization and loss rates, and eleven reaction channels; strictly positive ion temperature and mass ratio; both computed denominators finite and strictly positive

identity.relation: terminal H2+ density and temperature from explicit density, temperature and rate profiles
identity.direction: aligned x profiles and an eleven-channel reaction table -> four x profiles
identity.definition: For each spatial cell k, dissociation_frequency=neutral_density[k]*sum(reaction_rate_table[k,7:11]) and energy_exchange_frequency=(7.7e-7*neutral_density[k]*1e-6)/(sqrt(mass_ratio)*ion_temperature[k]^1.5), preserving the stated arithmetic order. The H2+ density denominator is dissociation_frequency+loss_frequency and must be finite and strictly positive. Molecular-ion density is molecular_density*neutral_density*ionization_rate divided by that denominator. Molecular-ion temperature is ion_temperature*energy_exchange_frequency divided by energy_exchange_frequency plus the density denominator; its denominator must also be finite and strictly positive.
identity.model: terminal molecular-ion algebraic state reduction with caller-supplied rate table
identity.geometry: one-dimensional spatial cell profiles; no velocity-grid input or iteration
identity.coordinates: all profiles share the same x-cell index; reaction table columns 7 through 10 use zero-based Python indexing
identity.boundary: finite aligned nonempty profiles; nonnegative molecular and neutral densities, ionization and loss rates, and eleven reaction channels; strictly positive ion temperature and mass ratio; both computed denominators finite and strictly positive
assumptions: The caller owns the eleven-channel reaction table and all state profiles. This callable does not assemble collision coefficients, generate an H2+ Maxwellian or iterate a terminal feedback loop.
Only channels 7:11 contribute to dissociation; changing the first seven table columns does not change these outputs.

The input names ionization_rate_s_inv and reaction_rate_table_s_inv are inherited from the historical interface, but their multiplication by neutral density leaves their physical dimensions unresolved. The numerical formula and the historical labels are preserved pending expert unit review.
Boolean, complex and numeric-string coercions are excluded by the maintained real-numeric contract.

inputs.name: molecular_density_m3
inputs.constraints: Finite, nonnegative, nonempty and one-dimensional; zero values are allowed if denominators remain positive.

inputs.name: neutral_density_m3
inputs.description: Caller-supplied neutral density used in dissociation and exchange terms.
inputs.constraints: Finite and nonnegative; one value per x cell.

inputs.name: ion_temperature_ev
inputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive; one value per x cell.

inputs.name: mass_ratio
inputs.description: Positive mass factor in the source energy-exchange frequency.
inputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive; boolean and numeric-string coercions are rejected.

inputs.name: ionization_rate_s_inv
inputs.description: Caller-supplied ionization-rate profile used in the H2+ density numerator.
inputs.units: source-labeled s^-1; density-scaled physical dimension unresolved
inputs.constraints: Finite and nonnegative; one value per x cell.

inputs.name: reaction_rate_table_s_inv
inputs.description: Eleven nonnegative reaction channels per x cell; columns 7:11 enter dissociation.
inputs.units: source-labeled s^-1; density-scaled physical dimension unresolved
inputs.constraints: Finite, nonnegative and exactly eleven columns in source order.

inputs.name: loss_frequency_s_inv
inputs.description: Caller-supplied loss frequency added to the dissociation denominator.
inputs.constraints: Finite and nonnegative; one value per x cell.

outputs.name: molecular_ion_density_m3
outputs.units: source-labeled m^-3; coefficient units pending review

outputs.name: molecular_ion_temperature_ev
outputs.constraints: Finite and nonnegative; zero is permitted when exchange vanishes.

outputs.name: dissociation_frequency_s_inv
outputs.description: Neutral density times the sum of reaction channels 7 through 10.
outputs.units: source-labeled s^-1; coefficient units pending review

outputs.name: energy_exchange_frequency_s_inv
outputs.description: Source-calibrated ion energy-exchange frequency with explicit 1e-6 density scaling.

preconditions: The caller supplies aligned terminal H2/neutral densities, ion temperature, rates and the eleven-column reaction table.
Dissociation plus loss and the temperature denominator remain finite and strictly positive in every cell.
supported: Stateless source-form H2+ density and temperature reduction on finite one-dimensional carriers.
excluded: Reaction-rate table construction, H2+ distribution seeding, kinetic collision closure, terminal feedback and external physical validation.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for non-real numeric or non-finite inputs, malformed profile/table shapes, negative densities or rates, nonpositive ion temperature or mass ratio, or a nonpositive/non-finite computed denominator.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError if any returned density, temperature or frequency becomes non-finite or negative; no partial mapping is returned.

python.signature: reduce_terminal_molecular_ion_state(molecular_density_m3, neutral_density_m3, ion_temperature_ev, mass_ratio, ionization_rate_s_inv, reaction_rate_table_s_inv, loss_frequency_s_inv)

example.description: Reduce two aligned terminal H2+ state cells from explicit rates.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.kinetic import reduce_terminal_molecular_ion_state
rates = np.zeros((2, 11))
rates[:, 7:11] = 1e-18
r = reduce_terminal_molecular_ion_state(np.array([4e17, 5e17]), np.array([1e18, 2e18]), np.array([2., 3.]), 2., np.array([4., 5.]), rates, np.array([1., 3.]))
assert set(r) == {'molecular_ion_density_m3', 'molecular_ion_temperature_ev', 'dissociation_frequency_s_inv', 'energy_exchange_frequency_s_inv'}
assert all(value.shape == (2,) and np.isfinite(value).all() for value in r.values())
example.expected: Four finite two-cell terminal H2+ profiles with source-order reaction channels.

scope: Independent per-cell oracle checks all four fields with nonuniform reaction channels.
First-seven-channel variation and zero molecular density preserve the stated boundaries.
Three digest-pinned fixed cases cover exact finite agreement and the boolean-coercion divergence.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Direct numerical comparisons establish the finite discrete algebraic relation and boundary differences on tested carriers. They do not establish rate-table provenance, absolute units, a full H2+ kinetic closure, complete qualification or expert approval.
known_limitations: Numerical agreement with the reference cases is bounded evidence and does not establish full qualification.
The density-scaled ionization/reaction-rate units and absolute H2+ density normalization require expert review.
